mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 5% for two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and compressing equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the effect reverses during a recession (UNRATE < 3%).

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a drop in housing starts (HOUST) indicates weakening consumer demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -2% AND HOUST monthly change < -10%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the relationship inverts during a supply shock.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in industrial production (INDPRO) above its 12-month moving average by more than 3% for three consecutive months signals improving manufacturing activity and corporate earnings momentum, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: INDPRO continues to rise but S&P 500 20-day returns are not statistically different from zero in more than 70% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate (UNRATE) falling below 4% while payroll employment (PAYEMS) grows at a pace above its 12-month average indicates a tight labor market, which pressures firms to raise wages and prices, ultimately reducing profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered months, or the effect disappears during periods of high inflation (CPIAUCSL YoY > 5%).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) below 2% accompanied by a concurrent increase in savings deposits (RSAFS) signals a liquidity trap environment, where monetary policy loses traction, resulting in muted S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
regime_hint: liquidity trap or zero lower bound
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the effect is not present during financial crisis periods.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in real personal savings (RSAFS) exceeding 5% while consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) is below 2% suggests households are saving rather than spending, which dampens demand and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS monthly change > 5% AND CPIAUCSL YoY < 2%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered months, or the effect reverses during a supply shock.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 3.5% for four consecutive months, with no corresponding acceleration in wage growth (implied by stable PAYEMS growth), indicates a mismatch between labor supply and demand, which historically precedes equity market corrections and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 3.5% for 4 consecutive months AND PAYEMS monthly change within ±0.2%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative in more than 70% of triggered episodes, or the effect is absent during periods of high inflation.

mechanism_narrative: A two-month consecutive acceleration in industrial production (INDPRO) above 4% signals robust manufacturing expansion, which typically boosts earnings expectations and supports higher equity valuations, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change > 4% for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are not significantly positive in more than 60% of triggered months, or the effect reverses during a demand shock.
